announcements.name: APUSH LEQ Practice (and The Presidents videos) Tuesday and Wednesday 9/22-23, Unit 3 MCQs (after review session) Thursday and Friday 9/24-25
announcements.directions: Here is another APUSH DBQ that you may want to use for practice. But, remember, for unit 3, your summative writing assessment is an LEQ. https://shshistory.com/extra%20pages/APAmericanHistory/ap%20essay%20guidelines/ap%20amhist%20essay%20guidelines.pdf LEQ Rubric- 1 point for background/context, 1 point for a thesis (with an argument and reasons), 2 points for evidence (6 strong examples in two or three body paragraphs), and 2 points for analysis (explanation and historical significance) Your class period will be assigned one of these three prompts (so study for both because you won't have a choice) for your first LEQ/traditional four or five-paragraph essay (40 minutes in class) on Tuesday or Wednesday, September 29th or 30th (odd/even day). Evaluate the relative importance of the following as factors prompting Americans to rebel in 1776: Parliamentary taxation, British military measures, restriction of civil liberties, the legacy of the colonial religious and political ideas. (1992 FRQ) Between 1783 and 1800, the new government of the United States faced the same political and economic issues that troubled the British government’s relations with the colonies prior to the Revolution. Assess the validity of this generalization. (1980 FRQ) Analyze the extent to which the American Revolution represented a radical alteration in American political ideas and institutions. (from AP Classroom) *Reminders: Be clear about who, what, when, where, and why as you integrate and analyze evidence. Maintain your argument, specificity (related key terms), citation (Doc 1), and chronological order throughout your essay. Review this unit 3 timeline. 1765 Stamp Act 1770 Boston Massacre 1773 Boston Tea Party 1776 Declaration of Independence 1783 Treaty of Paris 1786 Shays’ Rebellion 1787 Constitutional Convention 1790 Compromise/’Dinner Table’ Bargain 1794 Whiskey Rebellion 1798 Alien and Sedition Acts/XYZ Affair
